notes.front: What is a perfect square wave made of, in terms of harmonics?
notes.back: An infinite number of odd harmonics, all crossing the reference line in phase with the fundamental.
notes.explanation: Each odd harmonic added makes the sides of the composite waveform steeper, bringing it nearer a perfect square wave.
notes.example: Like a sine wave squared off at top and bottom: a 1 kHz square wave also carries 3 kHz, 5 kHz, 7 kHz and more.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 9, chapter 4, square waves, p. 4-32
notes.evidence: The addition of more odd harmonics will bring the composite waveform nearer the shape of the perfect square wave. A perfect square wave is, therefore, composed of an infinite number of odd harmonics. In the composition of square waves, all the odd harmonics cross the reference line in phase with the fundamental.

notes.front: What does Fourier analysis reveal about a waveform such as a square wave?
notes.back: The sine wave and harmonics it is made of: for a square wave, a sine wave and its odd harmonics.
notes.explanation: It is the analysis behind the Fast Fourier Transform, which DSP uses to move a signal from the time domain to the frequency domain.
notes.example: Like listing the notes in a chord, but for a waveform: a square wave breaks into a sine wave and its odd harmonics.
notes.evidence: E8A01 (A) What technique shows that a square wave is made up of a sine wave and its odd harmonics? A. Fourier analysis

notes.front: How is a signal described in the time domain?
notes.back: As its amplitude at different times.
notes.explanation: It is the view an oscilloscope gives: the waveform as it changes from moment to moment.
notes.example: Like a sound recording's waveform display, with amplitude up the side and time along the bottom.
notes.evidence: E8A03 (B) Which of the following describes a signal in the time domain? A. Power at intervals of phase B. Amplitude at different times

notes.front: How does a frequency-domain description of a signal differ from a time-domain one?
notes.back: It describes the signal by the frequencies it contains, not by its amplitude at different times.
notes.explanation: A Fast Fourier Transform is the tool that converts a signal from the time domain into the frequency domain.
notes.example: Like a graphic equaliser's bars, showing how much of the signal sits at each frequency.
notes.evidence: E7F07 (C) What function is performed by a Fast Fourier Transform? A. Converting analog signals to digital form B. Converting digital signals to analog form C. Converting signals from the time domain to the frequency domain

notes.front: In which direction does a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) convert a signal?
notes.back: From the time domain to the frequency domain.
notes.explanation: Its input is amplitude at different times; its output is the signal's frequency content.
notes.example: Like a prism splitting white light into colours, but done by calculation on sampled signal data.
notes.evidence: E7F07 (C) What function is performed by a Fast Fourier Transform? A. Converting analog signals to digital form B. Converting digital signals to analog form C. Converting signals from the time domain to the frequency domain

notes.front: Which kinds of signal can a true-RMS meter measure correctly?
notes.back: Both sinusoidal and non-sinusoidal signals: it calculates the RMS value of either.
notes.explanation: Its benefit is the calculation itself, not transforms, noise factors or phasor forms.
notes.example: Like an ordinary alternating-current voltmeter, but it still reads the right RMS value on a square wave.
notes.evidence: E8A05 (D) What is the benefit of making voltage measurements with a true-RMS calculating meter? A. An inverse Fourier transform can be used B. The signal’s RMS noise factor is also calculated C. The calculated RMS value can be converted directly into phasor form D. RMS is measured for both sinusoidal and non-sinusoidal signals

notes.front: What does the PEP-to-average ratio compare, and what is it for unprocessed SSB speech?
notes.back: Peak envelope power with average power; about 2.5 to 1 for unprocessed SSB phone.
notes.explanation: Speech characteristics set the ratio, not the modulating frequency, carrier suppression or amplifier gain.
notes.example: Like a runner's sprint speed against average pace: brief speech peaks sit above the average.
notes.evidence: E8A06 (A) What is the approximate ratio of PEP-to-average power in an unprocessed single-sideband phone signal? A. 2.5 to 1 B. 25 to 1 C. 1 to 1 D. 13 to 1 ~~ E8A07 (B) What determines the PEP-to-average power ratio of an unprocessed single-sideband phone signal? A. The frequency of the modulating signal B. Speech characteristics

notes.front: What does an analog-to-digital converter (ADC) do?
notes.back: It changes an analog voltage into digital information.
notes.explanation: In a digital multimeter, the signal-conditioning section feeds it a DC analog voltage that represents the input being measured.
notes.example: Like a digital multimeter's converter section, which turns a measured voltage into numbers.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 16, chapter 4, digital multimeters, p. 4-14
notes.evidence: The signal conditioning section provides a dc analog voltage, characteristic of the applied input, to the analog-to-digital converter section. This task is accomplished by the input voltage divider, current shunts, ac converter, active filter, and associated switching. The analog-to-digital (a/d) converter section changes the dc output voltage from the signal conditioning section to digital information.

notes.front: What is successive approximation, in converter terms?
notes.back: A type of analog-to-digital conversion.
notes.explanation: The pool names it as the ADC method, beside distractors such as level shifting and phase reversal.
notes.example: Like a game of twenty questions, as the name suggests: the answer is closed in on by successive tries.
notes.evidence: E8A02 (A) Which of the following is a type of analog-to-digital conversion? A. Successive approximation B. Harmonic regeneration C. Level shifting D. Phase reversal

notes.front: What is the defining advantage of a flash (direct conversion) ADC?
notes.back: Very high speed, which allows high frequencies to be digitised.
notes.explanation: That speed is why software defined radios use them; the pool rejects low power and coding immunity as the reason.
notes.example: Like a camera with a very fast shutter, catching an RF waveform before it has moved on.
notes.evidence: E8A08 (C) Why are direct or flash conversion analog-to-digital converters used for a software defined radio? A. Very low power consumption decreases frequency drift B. Immunity to out-of-sequence coding reduces spurious responses C. Very high speed allows digitizing high frequencies

notes.front: What does an ADC's resolution, given in bits, determine?
notes.back: How many different input levels it can encode: 8 bits give 256.
notes.explanation: Each input level needs its own binary code, and 8 bits make 256 different codes.
notes.example: Like the markings on a ruler: more bits give finer steps across the same range.
notes.evidence: How many different input levels can be encoded by an analog-to-digital converter with 8-bit resolution? A. 8 B. 8 multiplied by the gain of the input amplifier C. 256 divided by the gain of the input amplifier D. 256

notes.front: What is quantization noise, and what makes it smaller?
notes.back: The difference between a quantized wave and the original; more standard levels make the quantized wave closer to the original.
notes.explanation: Only an infinite number of levels would exactly duplicate the original analog waveform, so some error always remains.
notes.example: Like rounding every price to the nearest pound: each rounding leaves a small error.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 12, chapter 2, pulse-code modulation, p. 2-48
notes.evidence: From this you should see that the greater the number of standard levels used, the more closely the quantized wave approximates the original. This is also made evident by the fact that an infinite number of standard levels exactly duplicates the conditions of nonquantization (the original analog waveform).

notes.front: What is added to an ADC's input as dither, and for what purpose?
notes.back: A small amount of noise, to reduce quantization noise.
notes.explanation: Dither is deliberate: it is not a fault in the converter or a way of skipping samples.
notes.example: Like a faint background hiss fed in on purpose along with the signal.
notes.evidence: E8A04 (B) What is “dither” with respect to analog-to-digital converters? A. An abnormal condition where the converter cannot settle on a value to represent the signal B. A small amount of noise added to the input signal to reduce quantization noise

notes.front: What does a digital-to-analog converter (DAC) do, and what follows its output?
notes.back: It turns digital data back into an analog signal; a low-pass filter at its output removes spurious sampling artefacts.
notes.explanation: It is the reverse of the ADC, and its output still carries artefacts of the sampling process.
notes.example: Like the output stage of a digital audio player, turning stored numbers back into a voltage for headphones.
notes.evidence: What is the purpose of a low-pass filter used at the output of a digital-to-analog converter? A. Lower the input bandwidth to increase the effective resolution B. Improve accuracy by removing out-of-sequence codes from the input C. Remove spurious sampling artifacts from the output signal

notes.front: What does total harmonic distortion (THD) measure for an ADC?
notes.back: The converter's quality.
notes.explanation: The pool picks it over peak envelope power, reciprocal mixing and power factor, which measure other things.
notes.example: Like an amplifier's distortion figure, but quoted for a converter.
notes.evidence: E8A11 (A) Which of the following is a measure of the quality of an analog-to-digital converter? A. Total harmonic distortion

notes.front: What does a sample rate describe, and what does raising it do?
notes.back: How often the signal is sampled; a higher rate reproduces the original more accurately.
notes.explanation: The signal must be represented by enough pulses to restore its original shape, and sampling more often gives more of them.
notes.example: Like frames per second in video: more frames show movement more faithfully.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 12, chapter 2, pulse modulation, sampling rate, p. 2-41
notes.evidence: To ensure maximum fidelity (accuracy in reproducing a modulating wave), the modulating signal has to be represented by enough pulses to restore the original wave shape. Logically, the higher the sampling rate (the more often sampled) of the pulse modulator, the more accurately the original modulating wave can be reproduced.

notes.front: What is the Nyquist rate?
notes.back: The minimum sampling rate for accurate reproduction: twice the highest frequency in the signal.
notes.explanation: The Navy course calls two times the highest modulating frequency the minimum, and used 2.5 times as its standard rate.
notes.example: Like needing at least two snapshots per swing to see a pendulum's rate: a 5 kHz tone needs 10,000 samples a second or more.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 12, chapter 2, pulse modulation, sampling rate, p. 2-41
notes.evidence: View (C) shows a sampling rate that is two times the highest modulating frequency. This is the minimum sampling rate that will give a sufficiently accurate reproduction of the modulating wave. The standard sampling rate is 2.5 times the highest frequency that is to be transmitted.

notes.front: What is aliasing in a sampled system?
notes.back: High-frequency components being reproduced as lower-frequency components.
notes.explanation: On a digital oscilloscope it shows up as a false, jittery low-frequency version of the waveform.
notes.example: Like a wagon wheel in a film that seems to turn slowly backwards: the samples miss what really happened.
notes.evidence: E7F09 (A) Why is an anti-aliasing filter required in a decimator? A. It removes high-frequency signal components that would otherwise be reproduced as lower frequency components

notes.front: What does decimation do to a digital signal?
notes.back: It reduces the effective sample rate by removing samples.
notes.explanation: It changes the rate only: it is not a number-format conversion, an attenuator, or trimming of digits.
notes.example: Like keeping every tenth frame of a video: the clip still plays, at a lower frame rate.
notes.evidence: E7F08 (B) What is the function of decimation? A. Converting data to binary-coded decimal form B. Reducing the effective sample rate by removing samples

notes.front: What does an anti-aliasing filter remove?
notes.back: High-frequency components that would otherwise be reproduced as lower-frequency components.
notes.explanation: A decimator needs one, because lowering the sample rate would otherwise let those components alias.
notes.example: Like a sieve before the pot: it stops frequencies too high for the new rate before they can fold down.
notes.evidence: E7F09 (A) Why is an anti-aliasing filter required in a decimator? A. It removes high-frequency signal components that would otherwise be reproduced as lower frequency components

notes.front: What makes a software defined receiver 'direct sampling'?
notes.back: Incoming RF is digitised by an ADC without first being mixed with a local oscillator signal.
notes.explanation: There is no mixing stage before the converter, so the ADC works on the RF itself.
notes.example: Like photographing a scene directly rather than a print of it: no frequency conversion comes first.
notes.evidence: C. Incoming RF is digitized by an analog-to-digital converter without being mixed with a local oscillator signal

notes.front: What does it mean for two signals of the same frequency to be in quadrature?
notes.back: They are 90 degrees out of phase.
notes.explanation: DSP transmitters combine signals in this relationship to make SSB, and quadrature amplitude modulation is named after it.
notes.example: Like a sine and a cosine: the same frequency, one a quarter-cycle behind the other.
notes.evidence: Transmission of data by modulating the amplitude of two carriers of the same frequency but 90 degrees out of phase

notes.front: What is a Hilbert-transform filter used for in DSP?
notes.back: Generating an SSB signal.
notes.explanation: It works on the transmitting side, whereas an adaptive filter cleans noise from received audio.
notes.example: Like a balanced modulator and sideband filter, but done in software.
notes.evidence: E7F03 (C) What type of digital signal processing filter is used to generate an SSB signal? A. An adaptive filter B. A notch filter C. A Hilbert-transform filter

notes.front: What is an adaptive filter used for on received SSB?
notes.back: Removing unwanted noise.
notes.explanation: It is a DSP audio filter working on the receive side, unlike the Hilbert-transform filter that generates SSB.
notes.example: Like noise-cancelling headphones, but applied to a receiver's audio.
notes.evidence: E7F02 (A) What kind of digital signal processing audio filter is used to remove unwanted noise from a received SSB signal? A. An adaptive filter

notes.front: What is generally true of a finite impulse response (FIR) filter's delay?
notes.back: It can delay all frequency components of the signal by the same amount.
notes.explanation: The pool does not accept 'easier to implement' or 'faster to respond' as generally true; equal delay is the point.
notes.example: Like holding back every note of a chord by the same time, so the chord stays intact.
notes.evidence: E7F12 (A) Which of the following is generally true of Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filters? A. FIR filters can delay all frequency components of the signal by the same amount

notes.front: What are the taps of a DSP filter?
notes.back: Points that provide incremental signal delays for the filter algorithm.
notes.explanation: They are not debugging access or baseband selection points; adding more of them sharpens the response.
notes.example: Like the stops along a delay line, each one a step later than the last.
notes.evidence: What is the function of taps in a digital signal processing filter? A. To reduce excess signal pressure levels B. Provide access for debugging software C. Select the point at which baseband signals are generated D. Provide incremental signal delays for filter algorithms

notes.front: What happens if a signal is sampled at fewer than two samples per cycle?
notes.back: The original signal cannot be reproduced.
notes.explanation: So two samples per cycle of the highest frequency is the floor for any sampled system.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 12, chapter 2, pulse modulation, sampling rate, p. 2-41
notes.evidence: If less than two samples per cycle are made, you are not able to reproduce the original modulating signal, as shown in view (B).

notes.front: In the Navy course's pulse systems, what does a sampling rate above twice the modulating frequency cost?
notes.back: A wide bandwidth, and more average power from the transmitter.
notes.explanation: The gain is a very accurate reproduction of the modulating signal, so the trade is accuracy against bandwidth and power.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 12, chapter 2, pulse modulation, sampling rate, p. 2-41
notes.evidence: View (A) shows a sampling rate of more than two times the modulating frequency. As you can see, this reproduces the modulating signal very accurately. However, the high sampling rate requires a wide bandwidth and increases the average power required of the transmitter.

notes.front: What is meant by “direct sampling” in software defined radios?
notes.choices:
A) Software is converted from source code to object code during operation of the receiver
B) I and Q signals are generated by digital processing without the use of RF amplification
C) Incoming RF is digitized by an analog-to-digital converter without being mixed with a local oscillator signal
D) A switching mixer is used to generate I and Q signals directly from the RF input
notes.back: Incoming RF is digitized by an analog-to-digital converter without being mixed with a local oscillator signal
notes.choicesExplained: A: compiling software is unrelated. B: direct sampling is about leaving out mixing, not RF amplification. D: a switching mixer is still a mixer, which direct sampling leaves out.
notes.explanation: No local-oscillator mixing comes before the converter: the ADC digitises the incoming RF itself.
notes.evidence: What is meant by “direct sampling” in software defined radios?

notes.front: What kind of digital signal processing audio filter is used to remove unwanted noise from a received SSB signal?
notes.choices:
A) An adaptive filter
B) A crystal-lattice filter
C) A Hilbert-transform filter
D) A phase-inverting filter
notes.back: An adaptive filter
notes.choicesExplained: B: a crystal-lattice filter is built from quartz crystals, not DSP. C: a Hilbert-transform filter generates SSB. D: 'phase-inverting filter' is a distractor.
notes.explanation: Its task is noise on the received audio; the Hilbert-transform filter is the one that generates SSB.
notes.evidence: What kind of digital signal processing audio filter is used to remove unwanted noise from a received SSB signal?

notes.front: What type of digital signal processing filter is used to generate an SSB signal?
notes.choices:
A) An adaptive filter
B) A notch filter
C) A Hilbert-transform filter
D) An elliptical filter
notes.back: A Hilbert-transform filter
notes.choicesExplained: A: an adaptive filter removes noise from received SSB. B: a notch filter removes a narrow band of frequencies. D: an elliptical filter is a filter response type, not an SSB generator.
notes.explanation: A Hilbert-transform filter shifts every audio frequency by 90 degrees, giving the quadrature copy that the phasing method needs to cancel one sideband.
notes.evidence: What type of digital signal processing filter is used to generate an SSB signal?

notes.front: Which method generates an SSB signal using digital signal processing?
notes.choices:
A) Mixing products are converted to voltages and subtracted by adder circuits
B) A frequency synthesizer removes unwanted sidebands
C) Varying quartz crystal characteristics are emulated in digital form
D) Signals are combined in quadrature phase relationship
notes.back: Signals are combined in quadrature phase relationship
notes.choicesExplained: A: subtracting mixing products in adder circuits is not the DSP method. B: a frequency synthesizer generates frequencies; it does not remove sidebands. C: emulating quartz crystals is not how DSP makes SSB.
notes.explanation: Audio and carrier are each split into two copies 90 degrees apart and mixed; combining the two products makes one sideband add and the other cancel.
notes.evidence: Which method generates an SSB signal using digital signal processing?

notes.front: How frequently must an analog signal be sampled to be accurately reproduced?
notes.choices:
A) At least half the rate of the highest frequency component of the signal
B) At least twice the rate of the highest frequency component of the signal
C) At the same rate as the highest frequency component of the signal
D) At four times the rate of the highest frequency component of the signal
notes.back: At least twice the rate of the highest frequency component of the signal
notes.choicesExplained: A: half the rate gives less than one sample per cycle. C: once per cycle is still too few. D: four times works but is more than the minimum.
notes.explanation: Fewer than two samples per cycle cannot reproduce the original, so twice the highest frequency is the minimum.
notes.evidence: How frequently must an analog signal be sampled to be accurately reproduced?

notes.front: What is the minimum number of bits required to sample a signal with a range of 1 volt at a resolution of 1 millivolt?
notes.choices:
A) 4 bits
B) 6 bits
C) 8 bits
D) 10 bits
notes.back: 10 bits
notes.choicesExplained: A: 4 bits give 16 levels. B: 6 bits give 64. C: 8 bits give 256, too few for 1,000 steps.
notes.explanation: 1 V in 1 mV steps is 1,000 levels; 10 bits give 1,024 (2¹⁰), enough, while 8 bits give only 256.
notes.evidence: What is the minimum number of bits required to sample a signal with a range of 1 volt at a resolution of 1 millivolt?

notes.front: What function is performed by a Fast Fourier Transform?
notes.choices:
A) Converting analog signals to digital form
B) Converting digital signals to analog form
C) Converting signals from the time domain to the frequency domain
D) Converting signals from the frequency domain to the time domain
notes.back: Converting signals from the time domain to the frequency domain
notes.choicesExplained: A: analog-to-digital conversion is the ADC's job. B: digital-to-analog conversion is the DAC's job. D: frequency to time is the reverse direction.
notes.explanation: It takes amplitude at different times and yields the signal's frequency content.
notes.evidence: What function is performed by a Fast Fourier Transform?

notes.front: What is the function of decimation?
notes.choices:
A) Converting data to binary-coded decimal form
B) Reducing the effective sample rate by removing samples
C) Attenuating the signal
D) Removing unnecessary significant digits
notes.back: Reducing the effective sample rate by removing samples
notes.choicesExplained: A: binary-coded decimal is a number format. C: attenuation changes level, not rate. D: it is samples that are removed, not digits.
notes.explanation: Dropping samples lowers the effective sample rate; an anti-aliasing filter has to come first.
notes.evidence: What is the function of decimation?

notes.front: Why is an anti-aliasing filter required in a decimator?
notes.choices:
A) It removes high-frequency signal components that would otherwise be reproduced as lower frequency components
B) It peaks the response of the decimator, improving bandwidth
C) It removes low-frequency signal components to eliminate the need for DC restoration
D) It notches out the sampling frequency to avoid sampling errors
notes.back: It removes high-frequency signal components that would otherwise be reproduced as lower frequency components
notes.choicesExplained: B: the filter does not peak the response. C: it removes high, not low, frequencies. D: it does not notch out the sampling frequency.
notes.explanation: At the lower sample rate, high-frequency components would otherwise appear as lower-frequency ones.
notes.evidence: Why is an anti-aliasing filter required in a decimator?

notes.front: What aspect of receiver analog-to-digital conversion determines the maximum receive bandwidth of a direct-sampling software defined radio (SDR)?
notes.choices:
A) Sample rate
B) Sample width in bits
C) Integral non-linearity
D) Differential non-linearity
notes.back: Sample rate
notes.choicesExplained: B: sample width, with the reference voltage, sets the minimum detectable signal. C and D: non-linearity is not what the pool ties to bandwidth.
notes.explanation: The converter must sample at least twice the highest frequency it is to reproduce, so a faster sample rate allows a wider band.
notes.evidence: What aspect of receiver analog-to-digital conversion determines the maximum receive bandwidth of a direct-sampling software defined radio (SDR)?

notes.front: What sets the minimum detectable signal level for a direct-sampling software defined receiver in the absence of atmospheric or thermal noise?
notes.choices:
A) Sample clock phase noise
B) Reference voltage level and sample width in bits
C) Data storage transfer rate
D) Missing codes and jitter
notes.back: Reference voltage level and sample width in bits
notes.choicesExplained: A: clock phase noise is not the pool's answer. C: data transfer rate does not set sensitivity. D: missing codes and jitter are converter errors, not the floor the pool names.
notes.explanation: Reference voltage and sample width together set the smallest voltage step the converter can resolve, as in the bits-for-1-mV calculation.
notes.evidence: What sets the minimum detectable signal level for a direct-sampling software defined receiver in the absence of atmospheric or thermal noise?

notes.front: Which of the following is generally true of Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filters?
notes.choices:
A) FIR filters can delay all frequency components of the signal by the same amount
B) FIR filters are easier to implement for a given set of passband rolloff requirements
C) FIR filters can respond faster to impulses
D) All these choices are correct
notes.back: FIR filters can delay all frequency components of the signal by the same amount
notes.choicesExplained: B and C: the pool does not accept 'easier to implement' or 'faster response' as generally true. D: so 'all these' is wrong too.
notes.explanation: An FIR filter with symmetrical coefficients delays every frequency by the same time, so the waveform’s shape is kept; ease of design and speed are not generally true.
notes.evidence: Which of the following is generally true of Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filters?

notes.front: What is the function of taps in a digital signal processing filter?
notes.choices:
A) To reduce excess signal pressure levels
B) Provide access for debugging software
C) Select the point at which baseband signals are generated
D) Provide incremental signal delays for filter algorithms
notes.back: Provide incremental signal delays for filter algorithms
notes.choicesExplained: A: signal pressure is not a filter concept. B: taps are not debugging access. C: they do not select where baseband signals are generated.
notes.explanation: Taps supply the incremental delays the filter algorithm works with; more of them allow a sharper response.
notes.evidence: What is the function of taps in a digital signal processing filter?

notes.front: Which of the following would allow a digital signal processing filter to create a sharper filter response?
notes.choices:
A) Higher data rate
B) More taps
C) Lower Q
D) Double-precision math routines
notes.back: More taps
notes.choicesExplained: A: a higher data rate is not what sharpens it. C: lower Q means a broader response, not a sharper one. D: extra numeric precision is not the pool's answer.
notes.explanation: More taps give the algorithm more incremental delays to work with, and so a sharper response.
notes.evidence: Which of the following would allow a digital signal processing filter to create a sharper filter response?

notes.front: What technique shows that a square wave is made up of a sine wave and its odd harmonics?
notes.choices:
A) Fourier analysis
B) Vector analysis
C) Numerical analysis
D) Differential analysis
notes.back: Fourier analysis
notes.choicesExplained: B, C and D: vector, numerical and differential analysis are not the technique that splits a waveform into its harmonics.
notes.explanation: A perfect square wave is composed of an infinite number of odd harmonics, which Fourier analysis reveals.
notes.evidence: What technique shows that a square wave is made up of a sine wave and its odd harmonics?

notes.front: Which of the following is a type of analog-to-digital conversion?
notes.choices:
A) Successive approximation
B) Harmonic regeneration
C) Level shifting
D) Phase reversal
notes.back: Successive approximation
notes.choicesExplained: B: 'harmonic regeneration' is a distractor. C and D: level shifting and phase reversal do not turn an analog voltage into digital data.
notes.explanation: The converter compares the input with trial values, deciding one bit at a time from the most significant down, halving the remaining range at each step.
notes.evidence: Which of the following is a type of analog-to-digital conversion?

notes.front: Which of the following describes a signal in the time domain?
notes.choices:
A) Power at intervals of phase
B) Amplitude at different times
C) Frequency at different times
D) Discrete impulses in time order
notes.back: Amplitude at different times
notes.choicesExplained: A: power against phase is not a domain view. C: frequency at different times is not the time-domain description. D: discrete impulses describe samples, not the time domain itself.
notes.explanation: The time domain is the oscilloscope-style view, amplitude against time, as opposed to the frequency domain.
notes.evidence: Which of the following describes a signal in the time domain?

notes.front: What is “dither” with respect to analog-to-digital converters?
notes.choices:
A) An abnormal condition where the converter cannot settle on a value to represent the signal
B) A small amount of noise added to the input signal to reduce quantization noise
C) An error caused by irregular quantization step size
D) A method of decimation by randomly skipping samples
notes.back: A small amount of noise added to the input signal to reduce quantization noise
notes.choicesExplained: A: failing to settle would be a fault, not dither. C: irregular step size is a converter error. D: skipping samples is decimation, not dither.
notes.explanation: The small added noise is deliberate; its purpose is to reduce quantization noise.
notes.evidence: What is “dither” with respect to analog-to-digital converters?

notes.front: What is the benefit of making voltage measurements with a true-RMS calculating meter?
notes.choices:
A) An inverse Fourier transform can be used
B) The signal’s RMS noise factor is also calculated
C) The calculated RMS value can be converted directly into phasor form
D) RMS is measured for both sinusoidal and non-sinusoidal signals
notes.back: RMS is measured for both sinusoidal and non-sinusoidal signals
notes.choicesExplained: A: an inverse Fourier transform is not what the meter offers. B: it calculates RMS, not a noise factor. C: phasor conversion is not the benefit.
notes.explanation: A square wave, for example, is non-sinusoidal (a sine wave plus odd harmonics), and a true-RMS meter still gives its RMS value.
notes.evidence: What is the benefit of making voltage measurements with a true-RMS calculating meter?

notes.front: What is the approximate ratio of PEP-to-average power in an unprocessed single-sideband phone signal?
notes.choices:
A) 2.5 to 1
B) 25 to 1
C) 1 to 1
D) 13 to 1
notes.choicesExplained: B and D: 25 and 13 to 1 are far higher than unprocessed speech gives. C: 1 to 1 would mean a steady signal with no peaks above the average.
notes.explanation: Speech characteristics set the ratio; with no processing, peaks run about two and a half times the average.
notes.evidence: What is the approximate ratio of PEP-to-average power in an unprocessed single-sideband phone signal?

notes.front: What determines the PEP-to-average power ratio of an unprocessed single-sideband phone signal?
notes.choices:
A) The frequency of the modulating signal
B) Speech characteristics
C) The degree of carrier suppression
D) Amplifier gain
notes.back: Speech characteristics
notes.choicesExplained: A: the modulating frequency is not what sets it. C: carrier suppression is a property of SSB, not of the ratio. D: amplifier gain raises peak and average alike.
notes.explanation: The ratio comes from the nature of speech itself, not from the transmitter's settings.
notes.evidence: What determines the PEP-to-average power ratio of an unprocessed single-sideband phone signal?

notes.front: Why are direct or flash conversion analog-to-digital converters used for a software defined radio?
notes.choices:
A) Very low power consumption decreases frequency drift
B) Immunity to out-of-sequence coding reduces spurious responses
C) Very high speed allows digitizing high frequencies
D) All these choices are correct
notes.back: Very high speed allows digitizing high frequencies
notes.choicesExplained: A: low power consumption is not the reason. B: immunity to out-of-sequence coding is not the reason. D: only C is correct.
notes.explanation: Their very high speed lets them digitise high frequencies directly, which a software defined radio needs.
notes.evidence: Why are direct or flash conversion analog-to-digital converters used for a software defined radio?

notes.front: How many different input levels can be encoded by an analog-to-digital converter with 8-bit resolution?
notes.choices:
A) 8
B) 8 multiplied by the gain of the input amplifier
C) 256 divided by the gain of the input amplifier
D) 256
notes.choicesExplained: A: 8 is the number of bits, not of levels. B and C: the input amplifier's gain does not change how many codes exist.
notes.explanation: Each added bit doubles the number of codes: 2⁸ = 256.
notes.evidence: How many different input levels can be encoded by an analog-to-digital converter with 8-bit resolution?

notes.front: What is the purpose of a low-pass filter used at the output of a digital-to-analog converter?
notes.choices:
A) Lower the input bandwidth to increase the effective resolution
B) Improve accuracy by removing out-of-sequence codes from the input
C) Remove spurious sampling artifacts from the output signal
D) All these choices are correct
notes.back: Remove spurious sampling artifacts from the output signal
notes.choicesExplained: A: the filter is at the output, so it cannot change input bandwidth or resolution. B: out-of-sequence codes are not what it removes. D: only C is correct.
notes.explanation: The converter's output carries artefacts of the sampling process, and the low-pass filter takes them out.
notes.evidence: What is the purpose of a low-pass filter used at the output of a digital-to-analog converter?

notes.front: Which of the following is a measure of the quality of an analog-to-digital converter?
notes.choices:
A) Total harmonic distortion
B) Peak envelope power
C) Reciprocal mixing
D) Power factor
notes.back: Total harmonic distortion
notes.choicesExplained: B: peak envelope power is a transmitter power measure. C: reciprocal mixing is a receiver problem. D: power factor concerns alternating-current power.
notes.explanation: Total harmonic distortion shows how much the converter adds harmonics that were not in the input; the lower it is, the more faithful the conversion.
notes.evidence: Which of the following is a measure of the quality of an analog-to-digital converter?

notes.front: How many different input levels can a 12-bit ADC encode?
notes.choicesExplained: A: 12 is the number of bits, not levels. B: 144 squares the bit count. D: 1,024 is what 10 bits give.
notes.explanation: Each bit doubles the count: 8 bits give 256 (2⁸), so 12 bits give 2¹² = 4,096.
notes.evidence: How many different input levels can be encoded by an analog-to-digital converter with 8-bit resolution? A. 8 B. 8 multiplied by the gain of the input amplifier C. 256 divided by the gain of the input amplifier D. 256

notes.front: You must digitise a 0–2 V signal in 1 mV steps. What is the fewest bits the ADC can have?
notes.choicesExplained: A: 8 bits give 256 levels. B: 10 bits give 1,024 levels, enough for only about 1 V. D: 16 bits would work but are not the fewest.
notes.explanation: 2 V in 1 mV steps is 2,000 levels; 2¹⁰ = 1,024 is too few and 2¹¹ = 2,048 is enough.
notes.evidence: E7F06 (D) What is the minimum number of bits required to sample a signal with a range of 1 volt at a resolution of 1 millivolt? A. 4 bits B. 6 bits C. 8 bits D. 10 bits

notes.front: A direct-sampling receiver must digitise everything up to 30 MHz. What is the lowest sample rate that can reproduce it?
notes.choices:
A) 15 MHz
B) 30 MHz
C) 60 MHz
D) 120 MHz
notes.back: 60 MHz
notes.choicesExplained: A: half the highest frequency is far too slow. B: sampling at the highest frequency gives only one sample per cycle. D: four times would work but is not the lowest.
notes.explanation: The rate must be at least twice the highest frequency component: 2 × 30 MHz = 60 MHz.
notes.evidence: B. At least twice the rate of the highest frequency component of the signal

notes.front: An unprocessed SSB voice signal peaks at 100 W PEP. About what average power does it produce?
notes.choicesExplained: A: that would be a 1 to 1 ratio, with no peaks. C: an average cannot exceed the peak. D: that would be a 25 to 1 ratio.
notes.explanation: The ratio is about 2.5 to 1, so 100 W ÷ 2.5 ≈ 40 W average.
notes.evidence: E8A06 (A) What is the approximate ratio of PEP-to-average power in an unprocessed single-sideband phone signal? A. 2.5 to 1

notes.front: You need the RMS voltage of a square-wave clock signal. Which meter gives it directly?
notes.choices:
A) A true-RMS meter
B) Any meter, since RMS is the same for every waveform
C) An ohmmeter
D) A field strength meter
notes.back: A true-RMS meter
notes.choicesExplained: B: the pool's point is that a true-RMS meter handles non-sinusoidal signals, and a square wave is one. C: an ohmmeter measures resistance. D: a field strength meter measures RF fields, not a circuit's voltage.
notes.explanation: A square wave is non-sinusoidal, and a true-RMS meter measures RMS for both sinusoidal and non-sinusoidal signals.
notes.evidence: What is the benefit of making voltage measurements with a true-RMS calculating meter? A. An inverse Fourier transform can be used B. The signal’s RMS noise factor is also calculated C. The calculated RMS value can be converted directly into phasor form D. RMS is measured for both sinusoidal and non-sinusoidal signals

notes.front: An SDR lowers its sample rate by decimation before demodulating. What must it do to the signal first?
notes.choices:
A) Pass it through an anti-aliasing filter
B) Add dither
C) Convert it to binary-coded decimal
D) Amplify it
notes.back: Pass it through an anti-aliasing filter
notes.choicesExplained: B: dither reduces quantization noise at the ADC; it does not stop aliasing. C: decimation has nothing to do with binary-coded decimal. D: gain does not remove the components that would alias.
notes.explanation: Without the filter, high-frequency components would be reproduced as lower-frequency ones at the reduced rate.
notes.evidence: E7F09 (A) Why is an anti-aliasing filter required in a decimator? A. It removes high-frequency signal components that would otherwise be reproduced as lower frequency components

notes.front: A DSP CW filter is not steep enough to reject a nearby signal. Which change makes its response sharper?
notes.choices:
A) Add more taps
B) Use fewer taps
C) Add dither
D) Lower the audio gain
notes.back: Add more taps
notes.choicesExplained: B: fewer taps work the other way. C: dither reduces quantization noise; it does not shape the filter. D: gain changes level, not the filter's shape.
notes.explanation: More taps give the filter algorithm more incremental delays to work with, and the pool links that to a sharper response.
notes.evidence: E7F14 (B) Which of the following would allow a digital signal processing filter to create a sharper filter response? A. Higher data rate B. More taps

notes.front: Two upgrades are offered for a direct-sampling SDR: a faster ADC sample rate, or more bits per sample. Which widens the maximum receive bandwidth?
notes.choices:
A) The faster sample rate
B) More bits per sample
C) Both equally
D) Neither
notes.back: The faster sample rate
notes.choicesExplained: B: sample width, with the reference voltage, sets the minimum detectable signal instead. C: only the sample rate sets maximum bandwidth. D: the sample rate does set it.
notes.explanation: The pool ties maximum receive bandwidth to the sample rate of the analog-to-digital conversion.
notes.evidence: What aspect of receiver analog-to-digital conversion determines the maximum receive bandwidth of a direct-sampling software defined radio (SDR)? A. Sample rate

notes.front: How does a time-domain view of a signal differ from a frequency-domain view?
notes.back: Time domain: amplitude at different times. Frequency domain: the frequencies the signal contains.
notes.explanation: A Fast Fourier Transform converts the first view into the second.
notes.evidence: E7F07 (C) What function is performed by a Fast Fourier Transform? A. Converting analog signals to digital form B. Converting digital signals to analog form C. Converting signals from the time domain to the frequency domain

notes.front: In a DSP radio, how do the jobs of an adaptive filter and a Hilbert-transform filter differ?
notes.back: The adaptive filter removes noise from received SSB; the Hilbert-transform filter generates SSB.
notes.explanation: One works on the received audio, the other on the signal being transmitted.
notes.evidence: E7F02 (A) What kind of digital signal processing audio filter is used to remove unwanted noise from a received SSB signal? A. An adaptive filter B. A crystal-lattice filter C. A Hilbert-transform filter D. A phase-inverting filter ~~ E7F03 (C) What type of digital signal processing filter is used to generate an SSB signal?

notes.front: In a direct-sampling SDR, what does the sample rate set, and what do the reference voltage and sample width set?
notes.back: Sample rate sets the maximum receive bandwidth; reference voltage and sample width set the minimum detectable signal.
notes.explanation: One is about how often the converter samples, the other about how finely it resolves each sample.
notes.evidence: What sets the minimum detectable signal level for a direct-sampling software defined receiver in the absence of atmospheric or thermal noise? A. Sample clock phase noise B. Reference voltage level and sample width in bits
